_about: Authoritative EA schema for this project: the SUBSET of ArchiMate 3.2 that matches our documents, plus a dormant reserve of further types that can be switched on later. node_types = allowed graph nodes, edge_types = allowed relationships (each anchored to one of ArchiMate's closed set of 11 relationships), attributes = allowed node properties. Step 1b/3a extraction is governed by this; Step 4 validates every extracted edge against the allowed source->target triples here. `label` = the org-facing name, `synonyms` = keywords that recognize the concept in document text, `archimate_type`/`archimate_relationship` = the formal standard anchor, `note` = a pragmatic-mapping caveat to review.
_enabled_rule: Only types with `enabled: true` are used by extraction (Steps 1b/3a) and validation (Step 4). `enabled: false` types are DORMANT reserve — present so a document that needs them can be switched on without a code change, but ignored until then. This is what the admin UI toggles on/off per type.

_schema_growth.note: OFF (frozen schema). When OFF: a document concept that maps to no enabled type degrades to the generic `element`/`associated_with` fallback and is flagged, but the vocabulary never changes on its own and no human step is required. When ON (governed growth): unmapped concepts additionally land in a review list with an LLM-suggested type for an EA to approve, promoting a dormant type to enabled or adding a new one. Toggled from the admin UI; safe to flip either way (files are the system of record, the DB is a re-projection).

spec_source: ArchiMate 3.2 (The Open Group). Names cross-checked against Bizzdesign 3.2 concepts, ServiceNow ArchiMate shapes, Unicom System Architect, MEGA HOPEX (official spec is behind an Open Group login).

relationship_vocabulary._note: The complete closed ArchiMate relationship set. Every edge_type below must anchor to exactly one of these. An extracted edge that cannot map to one of these is almost certainly spurious.

structural.Composition: An element consists of one or more other elements (whole-part; parts cannot exist without the whole).
structural.Aggregation: An element groups one or more other elements (whole-part; parts can exist independently).
structural.Assignment: Allocation of responsibility, performance of behaviour, or deployment (active structure -> behaviour/structure).
structural.Realization: A more concrete element realizes (fulfils/implements) a more abstract one.

dependency.Serving: An element provides its functionality to another element.
dependency.Access: Behaviour/active-structure reads, writes, or read/writes a passive (data) element. access_types: read | write | read-write | access.
dependency.Influence: Weakest dependency; one element affects the achievement of a motivation element.

dynamic.Triggering: A temporal/causal control flow: one element triggers another.
dynamic.Flow: Transfer of information or value from one element to another.

other.Specialization: An element is a particular kind of another element.
other.Junction: Connector joining several relationships of the same type.

vendor.label: Vendor / Supplier
vendor.note: External Business Actor, distinguished from `department` only by role (supplier vs owner). 'In-house' is NOT a vendor and must be recorded as an attribute, never a node (see attributes.vendor).

data_entity.label: Data Entity
data_entity.note: TOGAF 'Data Entity' is logical; mapped to ArchiMate Data Object (application layer). If you later want a conceptual/business view, the alternative anchor is Business Object.

data_store.label: Data Store
data_store.note: A physical store (DB/file). Anchored to Artifact; could be System Software (DBMS) depending on granularity.

data_centre.label: Data Centre
data_centre.note: A data centre is a physical Facility; ArchiMate also offers the cross-layer Location element if you prefer a logical placement.

control.label: Security Control
control.note: Security controls map most naturally to Motivation Requirements (something the architecture must satisfy); Constraint is the alternative.

framework.label: Compliance Framework
framework.note: A framework (ISO 27001, NIST CSF...) groups controls. Anchored to Grouping; Driver is the alternative if you model it as external pressure.

element.label: Generic Element (fallback)
element.note: GENERIC FALLBACK — kept ON so no data is lost. The gap-analysis table's subject is a generic reference to an item defined elsewhere; such rows do NOT create new nodes (Step 4 reconciles them onto the existing subject by name, contributing only roadmap attributes). Also the landing type for any concept that matches no enabled node type when _schema_growth is OFF. Flagged for review either way.

business_service.label: Business Service
business_service.note: DORMANT reserve. A service the business exposes (distinct from the `application` that realizes it). Switch on if a document describes services as first-class, not just apps.

product.label: Product
product.note: DORMANT reserve. A coherent offering of services/passive elements with a contract. Switch on if a document organizes around products.

application_service.label: Application Service
application_service.note: DORMANT reserve. The behaviour an application exposes (vs the `application` component itself). Switch on if docs model APIs/services separately from systems.

technology_service.label: Technology Service
technology_service.note: DORMANT reserve. Infrastructure capability exposed to the application layer (e.g. 'messaging', 'storage'). Switch on for a technology-service view.

principle.label: Architecture Principle
principle.note: DORMANT reserve. A normative statement guiding the architecture (Motivation). Switch on if principle documents are ingested.

course_of_action.label: Course of Action / Initiative
course_of_action.note: DORMANT reserve. A strategic initiative/approach (Strategy layer). Useful for roadmaps/initiatives; today the 2027 Roadmap lives as a wiki THEME, not a node.

supplied_by.label: Supplied by
supplied_by.note: Direction follows the vendor SERVING the application; emitted as application->vendor for convenience.

supports.label: Supported by process
supports.note: REVIEW: emitted as capability->process named 'supports', but semantically the process serves (supports) the capability. Consider renaming to 'supported_by' or flipping direction in Step 4.

system_of_record.label: System of record
system_of_record.note: Semantically the application Accesses (masters) the data entity; emitted as data_entity->application. Step 4 may flip to application->data_entity to match Access direction.

stored_in.label: Stored in
stored_in.note: In ArchiMate the Artifact REALIZES the Data Object (data_store->data_entity). Emitted data_entity->data_store for convenience; reconcile direction in Step 4. Association is the looser alternative.

hosts.label: Hosts
hosts.note: Node deploys/hosts the application (Assignment of infrastructure to the deployed component).

located_in.label: Located in
located_in.note: The Facility/Location aggregates the nodes within it (data_centre aggregates node); emitted node->data_centre. Association is the looser alternative.

governed_by.label: Governed by framework
governed_by.note: The framework aggregates its controls (framework aggregates control); emitted control->framework.

associated_with.label: Associated with (generic fallback)
associated_with.note: GENERIC EDGE FALLBACK — kept ON so no relationship is lost. The landing type for a genuine relationship whose specific kind maps to no enabled edge type (when _schema_growth is OFF). Flagged for review; promote to a specific edge when the pattern recurs.

depends_on.label: Depends on
depends_on.note: DORMANT reserve, but HIGH VALUE for dependency/impact questions. Switch on when Step 3a starts extracting app-to-app dependencies from prose/diagrams. Until then such links fall back to `associated_with`.

sends_data_to.label: Sends data to
sends_data_to.note: DORMANT reserve. Directed information flow between systems/processes — key for data-lineage and impact. Switch on with the 3a flow pass.

reads_writes.label: Reads / writes data
reads_writes.note: DORMANT reserve. Application/process accessing a data entity (carry access_type read|write|read-write). Complements system_of_record; switch on with the 3a data-access pass.

triggers.label: Triggers
triggers.note: DORMANT reserve. Temporal/causal process control flow — for process-chain questions. Switch on with a process-flow pass.

composed_of.label: Composed of
composed_of.note: DORMANT reserve. Whole-part structure (e.g. the 'Fee Collection module' as part of a capability). Switch on if sub-component structure is modelled.

specializes.label: Specializes
specializes.note: DORMANT reserve. 'A is a particular kind of B', same-type only. Switch on for taxonomy/classification structure.

influences.label: Influences
influences.note: DORMANT reserve. Weakest dependency onto a motivation/goal element. Switch on if motivation (principles/goals) is ingested.

attributes._note: Properties recorded ON a node (ArchiMate 'properties'), never nodes themselves. `applies_to` lists the node types that may carry each.

role.note: Free text describing what the server does.

applies_to.note: Free text target of a control (e.g. 'All production systems').

vendor.note: Recorded as an attribute only when the value is not a real external supplier (e.g. 'In-house'); real vendors become supplied_by edges.

current_state.note: From the gap-analysis 'Current' column; attached to the reconciled subject.

gap.note: From the gap-analysis 'Gap' column; the roadmap delta.
